Secretary and a Vice-President, with Ray Hall, Ray Middleton and Doug Fotheringham elected to the committee. With the two Halls both laid off from racing it has been particularly pleasing to see the fine return to form of Bob Barnes.

Success depends as much on depth as quality and although stalwarts Charlie MacLennan and Doug Fotheringham raced for the second time that day Belgrave could only raise one walker eligible for the final event.

DOUG. FOTHERINGHAM

Doug Fotheringham, Bob Picton and Bob Coates all walked well to put Belgrave amongst the medals for the second year running. The spotlight however was on the superlative display of Wil Wesch who thrashed a much fancied Dave Watson to take the individual honours.

We also congratulate DOUG FOTHERINGHAM on being elected Chairman of the Race Walking Association, Southern Area Committee. How very pleased to see TOMMY GREEN with his wife at Wimbledon recently, when he started our 50th Annual Open Walk.

Barry Ingarfield and Doug Fotheringham, now there's two I can thrash - or can I ? After the One Hour I thought Len Duquemin's age had at last caught up on him but where is he now?right up there again far out of my failing sight.
Doug Fotheringham 45:13 with 8:10 allowance won the Handicap and Barry Ingarfield, a new signing from Ipswich, 45:59 with 8:40 allowance took third.
Wilf Wesch held off a slightly suspect Ken Easlea for a very strong win with Doug Fotheringham whipping round the hills to take the Handicap.

Doug Fotheringham was not on top form but finished second proving too strong for a fast improving Barry Ingarfield. Those two distance stalwarts Ray Hall and Pat Duncan did their best to screw each other throughout the race with Pat pulling away up the last hill " out of earshot ".
A very encouraging turnout for this traditional after-Christmas meeting. The faster boys obviously suffered less from Christmas although it was Doug Fotheringham who pulled out the suprise.
Barry Ingarfield confirmed his recent form with Doug Fotheringham and Bob Picton both supporting well. Newcomer from Ireland John Johnson failed to break 100 minutes but scored in the team.
Some safe walking from Barry Ingarfield and strong backing in the shape of John Bromley Doug Fotheringham and Bob Picton gave Belgrave an unexpected 2nd place in this 'Junior' championship.
In the Metropolitan Police '10' Mile championship Brian Ward finished 4th in 86:54 and Doug Fotheringham 8th in 89:29. It appears that Charles MacLennan did not finish, the question is DID HE START ?
Come the Barking-Southend, our first man home was John Morris, tenth in 5hrs. 42m. 35s., with Doug Fotheringham not far behind in 12th place (5hrs. 48m. 35s.).
Bob Picton showed just a little of what he could so easily be capable of in the Met. Police '7' and Bob Carter and Doug. Fotheringham were generally oblivious but present.

John Hall was with the leading pack for the first four miles despite a heavy cold, and he gallantly held on for 7th position with the race being won by K.Emsley of Steyning. Bob Picton was our second man home with Doug Fotheringham and Eric Stroud, in only his second race for the Club, behind him.

Paul Wiltshire put up a distinguished time and to quote one of the judges, "could be very good if he will get his arms right". Doug Fotheringham for the second week led home Eric Stroud, although Eric was walking better than his "Garnet" performance.
In 1965 the M.P.A.A. promoted a race on a lap course at Chigwell and amongst those to qualify was Doug. Fotheringham in 21:31:09 for badge No. 373.

Third place in a minor Scottish Championship ruled John Hall ineligible, a car accident put John Bromley on the side lines (delighted to see he's recovering from his injuries), the Irish had a demonstration so Doug.
John Keown was elected President of the Southern Race Walking Association at the A.G.M. on August 11th. At the same meeting Doug. Fotheringham was elected a Vice-President.
They were 6th Dave McMullen with 26:03, 9th Doug. Fotheringham with 26:30, 10th John Hall with 26:42, 13th Martin Bennett with 28:21 and 18th Joe Scamell with 30:14.
Good backing up by Tanner, Hall and Lewin enabled the Bels to reach 2nd team place, in fact it proved to be a good effort all round with 23 Belgraye starters and Doug.
Brighton vests were prominent then came John Hall and Ray Middleton and our next two men, one of whom would be our fourth scorer, were further back, Ron Day just having a small lead on Doug.

In his first attempt at the event, Richard Tanner reached a praiseworthy 4th in the Police Barking to Southend Walk with 5hrs 13mins 17secs. Doug. Fotheringham was 11th with 5:44 and Johnny Morris 19th with 5:54:07.

Their success at Woodford owes much to the excellent help provided by a small band of Belgravians under the leadership of Carl Lawton our hard working Walking Secretary. Amongst the officials who organised the race was Doug.

This was another best forgotten National, once again due to unavoidable absenteeism - Bob Picton had put his hand through a window. Carl finished 4th and Ray Middleton backed up with Ron Day and Doug. Fotheringham but it was only good for 7th.

The Cambridge Harriers Open is never one of the best supported races and as a result usually gives some of our 'B' men a chance. So it proved again with Doug. Fotheringham and Dave McMullen coming through for third team overall.

A slightly under distance 7 mile race at Chigwell on November 24th for the "Archer Cup" gave two of our Metropolitan Policemen an additional chance to air their legs. Doug Fotheringham placed 9th in 57:14 with Tim Thorogood one place behind in 58:30.

Doug Fotheringham got to the finish nine seconds ahead of Dave McMullen with "Bomber" Bromley backing up. Towards the front it was only in the closing stages that Carl Lawton pushed into second slot, overtaking Seddon (BoE) and holding Greasley (Sheffield) at bay by four seconds.
Ron Day collected the "Horwood Cup" by getting to the finish one second ahead of Doug Fotheringham and Cecil Gittins took the handicap from John Moullin.
A bit of a gap then in came Doug Fotheringham who has been involved in Garnet races for about twenty years! So we were the first club to have their four in.

We had plenty of non-scoring backing including our three remarkable veterans Dave McMullen, John Dunsford and Doug Fotheringham. Our Newham AC member, Mike Scamell, continues to improve, as shown by his consistant high placings.

The 100 mile relay was well supported by Belgrave although there was the possibility of there being 2 teams starting, this fell through and we only just managed to start one and that was due to Doug Fotheringham stepping in at less than 24 hours notice.

At 10Km he was timed at 44:30, over a minute up on Seddon, and in torrential rain he drew even further away to set a new personal best of 91:01. Ray Middleton was 15th in 100:37 with Doug. Fotheringham also in the field but Carl had to retire due to back trouble.
Carl Lawton was also on the road again, this time winning the men's 10Km from the redoubtable Roger Mills - 45:38 to 46:07. Doug Fotheringham was 13th in 53:18.
The event was once again efficiently organised by Doug Fotheringham (who also competed) and it is an event where one often meets old friends.

…ceive one whole bottle each, second team half a bottle each and third team quarter of a bottle each. Congratulations to Doug. Fotheringham on being elected President of the Southern Area of the Race Walking Association.…

One other Belgravian had to make a trip to the prize table - Doug Fotheringham who took 8th individual handicap prize. The prizes were handed out by our President, Ray, and it was good to see the affection and goodwill which he enjoys amongst the race-walkers.
One notable absentee from the Belgrave line-up was Doug. Fotheringham, President of the Southern R.W.A. who could hardly complete in an event for which he was referee and starter.

With eight handicap prizes to compete for, our other walkers had plenty to go for and the ever consistent Doug Fotheringham was rewarded with 2nd place, Steve Marshall 4th and John Dunsford (with Doug preparing for their trip to New Zealand) 8th.
As usual we had good performances from our others, our Vets, led by World Champion Doug Fotheringham with John Bromley and Joe Scammell would surely have beaten any other Clubs trio.

Belgrave Vets won the British Team Championship at Leicester on October 19th with John Dunsford, Doug Fotheringham and John Bromley. In a one-hour Track Walk at Austin (Texas) in November, the winner was John Knifton with a distance of 7 miles 1698 yards, some three quarters of a mile ahead of the second man.

Doug Fotheringham, John and Barbara Dunsford were Belgrave trio in these games, all of whom had to pay their own way out and back. In the Womens, Barbara was 2nd in her age group with 38.00 in the 5 Kms. and 74.54 in the 10 Kms.
